title: Older Than Stonehenge by 6,000 Years
description: Göbekli Tepe: giant carved pillars raised before farming, writing or the wheel.

scenes.narration: This place is so old, it changed the story of civilisation.
scenes.image_prompt: circle of giant T-shaped carved stone pillars on a hilltop at dusk, prehistoric

scenes.narration: More than eleven thousand years ago, in what is now southern Turkey, hunter-gatherers gather on a hilltop.
scenes.image_prompt: prehistoric hunter-gatherers in animal skins gathering on a hill at sunset, campfires

scenes.narration: They raise huge T-shaped stone pillars, some over five metres tall.
scenes.image_prompt: prehistoric people using ropes and wooden levers to raise a huge T-shaped stone pillar

scenes.narration: The pillars are carved with foxes, boars, snakes and vultures.
scenes.image_prompt: close up of ancient stone pillar carved with fox, boar and snake reliefs, torchlight

scenes.narration: This was before farming. Before writing. Before the wheel.
scenes.image_prompt: wild landscape of upper Mesopotamia, wild grasses, gazelles, prehistoric hunters

scenes.narration: It's thousands of years older than Stonehenge and the pyramids.
scenes.image_prompt: split scene: Stonehenge and Egyptian pyramids small in the distance, ancient stone circle in front

scenes.narration: Later, the enclosures were buried, which helped preserve them.
scenes.image_prompt: archaeologists excavating stone pillars from earth under a modern protective roof

scenes.narration: Who built it, and why, is still debated. What do you think it was for?
scenes.image_prompt: Göbekli Tepe stone circles at golden hour, wide view
